children: Chevron Corp. (CVX, Financials), one of the world's biggest integrated energy producers, is among the U.S. oil corporations warning that global fuel markets have entered a tougher time.
Executives at major oil producers such as Chevron have warned that a worldwide gasoline crisis has arrived, as supply fears clash with ongoing demand.
Tighter markets can help crude prices, refining margins and cash generation for oil producers. That makes the warning potentially big for Chevron and Exxon Mobil.
Both corporations have spent years emphasizing the value of capital discipline above seeking output expansion at any cost.
A long spell of tight supply may add to the economics of that method. The opposite half of the equation is present.
At some point energy prices become an issue if they rise high enough to hurt consumer spending, increase transportation costs and push inflation higher.

That can potentially complicate interest rate decisions for central banks. So investors have an odd set-up. The same factors that are buoying oil-company earnings could also weigh on the broader economy.

For Chevron and Exxon stockholders, the next indication will be whether supply limitations continue to keep crude and refined-product prices high, or whether sluggish economic activity starts to undermine demand.

title: Chevron CEO warns a global fuel crisis is already here
